name: Archer Push-Up
description: The archer push-up is an advanced unilateral push-up variation where the body shifts laterally over one working arm while the opposite arm extends to the side for balance. This concentrates the pressing load onto a single side of the pectoralis major and triceps, serving as a progression toward the one-arm push-up.

execution.starting_position: Start in a wide push-up position with hands placed much wider than shoulder-width apart. Fingers point outward at a slight angle. Body is in a straight plank line.
execution.setup_instructions: Ensure adequate space on each side. Hands should be significantly wider than a standard push-up.
steps: Step 1: Begin in a wide push-up position with hands significantly wider than shoulder-width.
Step 2: Shift your bodyweight laterally over your right hand, bending the right elbow to lower your chest toward the right hand.
Step 3: As you lower to the right, the left arm extends straight with a slight bend, acting as a support and balance arm.
Step 4: Press through the right palm to return to the start, then shift to the left side. Alternate each repetition.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale as you lower to one side; exhale as you press back to center.
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips as the body shifts — keep the pelvis square
Bending the extended arm excessively, which reduces unilateral loading
safety_considerations: Build prerequisite strength with standard and wide push-ups before attempting this variation
Stop if you feel shoulder joint pain — this movement demands significant shoulder stability
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lower until the chest is at hand level on the working side, then press back to the top.
coaching_cues: Shift your center of mass directly over the working arm
Keep hips level — no rotation as you move side to side
